📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 19:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 02:46 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed his stint with the Ukrainian national team for the failed doping test which cost him two years of his career and revealed how fighting his case personally cost him millions of pounds.
  • The Chelsea winger, who is now on loan with Tottenham Hotspur, has opened up for the first time since he returned to football in the summer when his suspension was suddenly lifted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 19:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 02:46 EST, 19 November 2026.

Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed his stint with the Ukrainian national team for the failed doping test which cost him two years of his career and revealed how fighting his case personally cost him millions of pounds.

The Chelsea winger, who is now on loan with Tottenham Hotspur, has opened up for the first time since he returned to football in the summer when his suspension was suddenly lifted.

It was in a two-hour interview with Ukrainian journalist Dmitry Gordon via his YouTube channel. While the title of the video mentions ‘suicidal thoughts’, Mudryk clarifies during the conversation that he did not consider committing suicide despite being in a dark place. ‘Kill myself – no, that’s not a way out,’ he noted when asked that question.

But he did discuss how Chelsea broke the news of his failed test to him, whether they helped their £89million signing from Shakhtar Donetsk during his ban, his belief that the drug meldonium entered his system while he was in Ukraine, and why he is now with Tottenham. He further claimed that he has faced threats from gangsters, and admitted his dream is to someday win the Ballon d’Or.

On the Ukrainian national team and their federation, the Ukrainian Association of Football, Mudryk said: ‘I’ll be honest, it pretended to help. But in reality, there was no help. They created more problems than they solved. Especially when we needed help the most, they turned their backs on us.

'I just would like, for the future, everyone to understand that you can only rely on yourself.'.

Mykhailo Mudryk has spoken publicly for the first time about the doping case that cost him two years of his career.

Mudryk has criticised the Ukrainian Association of Football over their support during his case.

Daily Mail Sport contacted the Ukrainian Association of Football for comment.

Sources indicate that continuing, Mudryk mentioned: ‘The UAF is afraid of being left to blame in this situation, and afraid of the criticism or whatever else might come raining down. Distancing themselves from their own player, not helping, pretending to help, and in the end, first they drag the case out for months without really helping the case in the end. But at least the UAF isn’t to blame.’.

It has been revealed that mudryk was handed an initial four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test, with his last appearance prior to that coming in November 2024 in the Conference League away at Heidenheim. He scored in that 2-0 win for Chelsea. He was able to return when a seismic resolution was struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'. Mudryk appeared for Chelsea during their pre-season tour before joining Tottenham on loan.

On how and why he failed his test, Mudryk said: ‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium, never seen it, never come across it in my life. I only learned about it when they told me the news. I definitely have ideas. It’s a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe.

Sources indicate that ‘This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that’s Ukraine. There are no such drugs in England. It supposedly stimulates your heart and helps you, as far as I understand, handle physical load better.

‘I was at home and Chelsea’s management came to see me and they said we needed to talk. Then they say you’ve returned a positive doping test and now you’re facing a ban.

‘You can’t believe it’s true. You can’t believe this is happening to you. If I’d ever taken anything anywhere, I’d have understood that this conversation might happen one day.

‘At least I’d have understood it was possible. But when you spend a huge pile of money on watching your diet, on a nutritionist, on a chef. When you spend that much money every year on all these things, that’s the last thing you expect. Because it speaks for itself: that you take things very seriously, like nutrition, everything that goes into your body, you watch it very closely.

According to recent reports, ‘Otherwise there’d be no need to spend money on it, because you could manage without it. They tell you this news, and you sit there, and you kind of listen to them but don’t hear them.

Mudryk returned to action when his ban was lifted in August, with the winger revealing Xabi Alonso told him to get game time and that he was 'counting on him'.

The Ukrainian joined Tottenham on loan but has seen injury restrict his involvement to date.

According to recent reports, ‘At some point you just go into a trance. It feels like you’re falling in a dream off a skyscraper. You’re flying down, you feel yourself flying down, and only in a dream do you wake up when you hit the ground, but in real life you don’t wake up, you just keep falling. It hits you very hard mentally. At that moment the tears came later.’.

Mudryk revealed how ‘the figure is in the millions’ when asked about the lawyers fees which were needed to fight his case. He confirmed he paid for that himself, along with the personal trainers and massage therapists he used to maintain his fitness while suspended. However, Mudryk did add that Chelsea continued to pay his salary during his time out of football.

On joining Tottenham and being reunited with Roberto De Zerbi, who formerly managed him at Shakhtar Donetsk, Mudryk mentioned: ‘It’s a perfectly logical decision. The club (Chelsea) has a upcoming coach (Xabi Alonso), he sees football his own way. He sees the players he needs for that football. He came up and told me straight to my face: “You’d better go and play, get some game time, and then come back to Chelsea. I’m counting on you.”’ On De Zerbi, he added: ‘We met and he says: “Are you happy? Come on, we’ve still got a lot of work to do together.”’.

Mudryk added how difficult it was after switching to England and, along with encountering issues with his former representatives who encouraged him to move to Chelsea rather than Arsenal, he said: 'They give you ultimatums, you know. That’s how it is.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:31, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 07:32.

Chelsea have seen their hopes of signing Juventus youngster Kerim Alajbegovic hit a major stumbling block ahead of the January transfer window.

The Blues were previously interested in the teenager during the summer, with Blues boss Xabi Alonso having monitored his development closely during his time in charge of Bayer Leverkusen.

However, Juventus are determined to keep hold of the highly-rated winger, with a potential departure presently considered off the table.

Alajbegovic was pursued by Chelsea during the summer after impressing at RB Salzburg, but the west London club's proposed project failed to convince the youngster.

The Blues were understood to be considering sending him out on loan rather than offering immediate first-team opportunities, allowing the Serie A giants to secure his signature instead.

There has now been renewed interest from Alonso's side, but reports in Italy (via Sport Witness) suggest Chelsea face an uphill battle to bring the 19-year-old maestro to Stamford Bridge.

It is claimed that Alajbegovic 'isn't leaving' Juventus, with the Italian side pleased by his development and unwilling to consider an exit despite interest from England.

The £30m teenager is also happy with his role in Turin, where he believes he has the right environment to continue developing, with similar reports suggesting that he wants to remain at Juventus for a 'long time'.

As a result, an immediate departure has been described as 'truly barred', making a January transfer particularly difficult to negotiate.

Chelsea's interest is understandable given the Bosnian's potential, but the club may struggle to convince him that Stamford Bridge is the right place for his development.

Regular first-team football should be a priority for a teenager at this stage of his career, and Juventus are currently providing him with opportunities to establish himself.

By contrast, Chelsea's sizeable squad creates greater competition for attacking positions, with even highly-rated youngster Estevao having experienced his own difficulties securing consistent game time.

That situation could serve as a warning to Alajbegovic, particularly when he is already enjoying an increasingly prominent role in Turin.

Although Juventus may not offer the most stable environment, they are giving the youngster opportunities to develop at senior level.

Chelsea might be able to offer a lucrative project, but unless they can guarantee a clearer pathway into the first team, Alajbegovic would arguably be better off remaining in Italy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:51.

Tottenham Hotspur are considering a 'surprise' move for Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap as Roberto De Zerbi looks to strengthen his attacking options.

The 23-year-old has revived his career at the City Ground following a difficult spell at Chelsea, attracting renewed interest from north London.

However, a potential deal could be more complicated than initially expected, with Forest placing a substantial valuation on their summer signing.

According to FootballTransfers, Delap is 'admired' by De Zerbi, with Spurs continuing to monitor the former Ipswich Town forward after tracking him during the summer transfer window.

Delap has scored three goals in his first nine Premier League appearances for Forest, offering encouraging signs following his disappointing spell at Stamford Bridge.

A January move is considered extremely difficult, though, given Forest only signed him in the summer and are unlikely to sanction his departure while fighting for their Premier League status.

Tricky Trees owner Evangelos Marinakis is not expected to approve a mid-season sale, although it is understood that De Zerbi could be prepared to wait until the summer of 2027.

Forest are likely to demand around £75m for the Englishman, which would represent a significant profit on the initial £45m they paid Chelsea.

There is no denying that Delap has shown some improvement at Forest, but his overall Premier League goalscoring record remains a significant concern amid Spurs' renewed interest.

His three goals this season take his career total to just 16 efforts in 76 Premier League outings, while he managed only three goals in 47 appearances for Chelsea.

Those numbers hardly suggest a striker capable of immediately resolving Tottenham's attacking problems, particularly if Forest demand £75m to part with him.

Spurs still need a reliable source of goals if they are to climb the table and compete for major honours, rather than another expensive gamble on potential.

De Zerbi's admiration is understandable, but Tottenham should be wary of paying a premium for a forward whose top-flight returns remain underwhelming.

Delap may yet develop into an excellent striker, but spending that much on him would represent a considerable risk for a club with more pressing needs.

It has been revealed that it was actually the first competitive home game that Guimarães had played for Arsenal since his transfer from Newcastle United, as a result of a few niggles and the club’s unusual run of four consecutive away matches before the international break. The most recent of those was the 3-0 thrashing by Brighton, which was one of their worst defeats of the last few seasons.

This gritty victory represented a necessary response to that defeat, even if the performance was far from dominant. “We had a point to prove,” mentioned Arteta. “Something was touched in our identity against Brighton.”.

Guimarães, too, clearly felt that some wrongs needed to be made right. For all his brilliance in this game and against Sunderland, he had produced a horrible showing at the Amex Stadium a few weeks ago. “He was not at that level against Brighton,” remarked Arteta. “This is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action you have to be at that level. At Brighton, he wasn’t. Today, he was much better.”.

Leeds had not lost in their opening five Premier League matches of this season and it was easy to see why. They were willing to press Arsenal high up the pitch, taking risks and engaging in physical duels, and the strategy proved hugely effective for an hour.

In a recent development, if they had been more precise in the final third, they could have been a few goals ahead by the time Justin converted Gabriel Gudmundsson’s left-wing cross after 55 minutes. Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

Recent findings suggest that it was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Sources indicate that arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

A report in Brazil has claimed that AC Milan have made an offer to Real Madrid for Endrick, and it is for a permanent deal.

In the past few weeks, there has been a lot of speculation suggesting that Milan are lining up a winter move for Endrick. He seems to be a player that the owner Gerry Cardinale personally likes, and the funds are available to at least make an attempt.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that according to Vitor Sergio of TNT Sports Brazil, Milan have begun talks with Madrid and Endrick’s representatives and are expected to submit a total offer of €70m for him. This would be €60m in fixed money, and €10m in add-ons. He adds that a loan is ‘off the table’.

In addition, the Rossoneri know they need to substantially increase the Brazilian’s salary. He currently receives around €3.2m net per season. Milan are aware of the figures involved in this deal and believe they have the financial capacity to pursue it.

To seal the deal, Real Madrid would also reportedly ask for two clauses with the future in mind. The first would given them the option to buy Endrick back for €85m (with only the length of the buy-back window still to be decided).

The second would allow Real to match a future offer, with the aim of reducing the chances of Endrick joining Barcelona or another elite European club in the future.

Although Los Blancos are willing to negotiate with the Diavolo, the Spanish club remains uncertain about selling the 20-year-old, as Mourinho still wants to count on him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, west Ham’s veteran midfielder has been the subject of an honest interview in his home country on Czech radio coinciding with the release of his autobiography. One of the more revealing comments Tomas Soucek made concerns the pressure and the expectation of playing in front of a major audience – such as West Ham will undoubtedly face tomorrow as the season re-commences with a home tie at London Stadium in front of 60,000 expectant supporters.

In a recent development, unlike several others, from his words it is clear that Soucek seems to thrive on the pressure and the weight of expectation upon him. As one of only a handful of medal winners still at the club from the 2023 campaign, Soucek’s experience should become a steadying influence in the dressing room even though he mostly starts games on the bench these days.

Handling the weight of expectation at London Stadium has been daunting at times.

‘Tornado Tom’ reveals that, far from letting it get to him, he actually enjoys the weight of expectation and pressure :.

Sources indicate that “Yes, obviously I feel it, but I like the pressure. Because football is always up and down, you have so many wins and so many losses – and it’s up to you how you recover from all of it.

Recent findings suggest that “And I love that. As you stated, it’s the most watched league in the world. And West Ham’s fans are crazy – they’re the best in the league, and it’s such a historic club.

“From the first day until now, I think me and West Ham connection is as good as it could possibly be in all aspects.

“And, yes, the pressure is there, but I try to work with it – and that’s why we play football.” (englishradio.cz).

The pressure will be significantly eased with a clean sheet and three points tomorrow – whether Soucek now, 31 gets into the action or simply acts as a calming figure in the dressing room.   • The then United Head Coach had told the Newcastle United hierarchy in early July at the beginning of pre-season that he had decided to leave.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is now coming up to four months since Eddie Howe officially left Newcastle United.

The then United Head Coach had told the Newcastle United hierarchy in early July at the beginning of pre-season that he had decided to leave.

Eddie Howe though willing to hold the fort until the club had found his successor.

Sources indicate that with Matthias Jaissle having reached agreement to join Newcastle United, Eddie Howe officially exited on 31 July 2026. Al-Ahli messed NUFC around by delaying the necessary paperwork, which delayed Jaissle’s official appointment until 5 August 2026.

In these last almost four months, nothing has been heard of Eddie Howe, other than speculation on which job he might step into next, Manchester United the main target of speculation until Mauricio Pochettino was revealed.

Eddie Howe a subject lesson when it comes to how managers can behave if they want to step out of the spotlight when leaving a job, rather than choosing to turn up doing countless media appearances and interviews in a desperate attempt to appear relevant.

We have now though learnt a little about what Eddie Howe has done since leaving Newcastle United, though it hasn’t come from the man himself.

The Daily Echo has revealed that Eddie Howe has relocated back down to the south coast.

Then in a further update, it has been revealed that the former United boss has visited Staplewood, the Southampton training ground, to observe the Saints training during the international break and also talk to their manager.

Tonda Eckert has just signed a upcoming contract with Southampton taking him up to 2029, afterwards he spoke to the Daily Echo: “I talked to Eddie Howe a bit about how his journey was, as he started as a head coach, for example, very early on. I started as an assistant, and then you get to see the game out of different eyes, and you need to be able to change rapidly. If there’s a change of manager, obviously you have some own ideas, but in the way that you talk about the game, you need to be able to do that in the language that a manager sees the game in. I think I’ve been lucky to work with some top managers, very different ones, different nationalities, different leagues and then you go through the official stages with the federations to finish your Pro Licence. At that point, I think 15 years into the job, at one point you feel ready to get your ideas out and I’ve had the chance to go into first team football before I came here. I decided not to do that and take the first steps here with the under-21s because it’s always different.”.

When Eddie Howe left Bournemouth in August 2020, he spent 15 months taking time out with his family and a period of reflection. He also used the time to visit numerous clubs in the UK and overseas to observe their training and talk to their managers, adding to his knowledge and experience. Then in November 2021 he eventually took the job at Newcastle United and did an incredible job.

No matter what was claimed in the media, I doubted very much that Eddie Howe had any interest in taking the Manchester United job, or indeed any other job at this moment in time.

I think he will enjoy his time off with family, recharge his batteries, come back into management when he feels he is ready.

I am not saying it will be a 15 months wait this time but I would be amazed if he took another job within the next few months.

Wherever he ends up I can only wish him the very best.

By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 08:09.

Saturday night entertainment in the Bundesliga will come from the Veltins Arena in Gelsenkirchen, as Schalke 04 welcome Stuttgart for a tasty league encounter.

The hosts have endured a dreadful start to the season and are still looking to score their first home goal, while the visitors are setting their sights on a third successive league success.

Schalke ended their five-match goalless run last time out against Hoffenheim, although their attacking breakthrough counted for little as they suffered a 2-1 defeat.

That result left Die Konigsblauen sitting in the relegation zone during the international break, while head coach Miron Muslic avoided an early sack.

Nevertheless, the 44-year-old remains under considerable pressure, with Schalke now enduring a seven-game winless streak across all competitions.

Even more concerning for the Royal Blues faithful is the fact that their points tally after nine Bundesliga matches is identical to the one they recorded at the same stage of their disastrous 2022-23 campaign, which ended in relegation.

In order to turn things around, the hosts will need to start scoring goals, otherwise they risk becoming just the second team in Bundesliga history to go without a goal across their first five home matches of a season.

There is one positive for the hosts and that is the fact they beat Stuttgart when these two teams last met back in February 2023 - their only victory over the Swabians in five previous meetings.

While Schalke are on the ropes, Stuttgart are on the attack, with the Swabians looking to record their third straight Bundesliga win.

Sebastian Hoeness and his side powered to a 1-0 win over Werder Bremen just before the international break, leaving them just six points adrift of the top four.

Given their sluggish start to the campaign, Stuttgart's recent upturn represents a welcome change in fortunes, with their defensive improvements playing a significant role.

Two clean sheets from their last three domestic outings make for much better reading than the two shutouts they managed across their opening 10 matches of the season.

Stuttgart will now turn their attention to landing their first league win over Schalke since 2021 - the only success over the Royal Blues they boast in 12 previous meetings.

What’s more, the Swabians have not managed to win at the Veltins Arena since 2013 - losing four and drawing three of their last seven trips to Gelsenkirchen.

Stuttgart form (all competitions):.

Along with their goalscoring problems, Schalke are also dealing with a lengthy injury list.

Maximilian Wober and youngster Luca Vozar are both currently out with hamstring injuries.

Defender Timo Becker picked up a foot problem just before the international break, and will also remain on the sidelines.

Emil Hojlund is yet to feature for Schalke this season due to an Achilles injury, while midfielder Ron Schallenberg is out with a leg problem.

Stuttgart are also missing a handful of names, including midfielder Angelo Stiller who is struggling with an adductor injury.

Swiss defender Luca Jaquez featured in the 1-0 win over Bremen before the international break, but he has since become a doubt due to a ribs problem.

Youngsters Jarzinho Malanga and Justin Diehl complete the injury list, with the two players carrying thigh and abdominal concerns.

Meanwhile, forward Deniz Undav missed out on selection for the German national team, with the 30-year-old still looking for his first Bundesliga goal this season.

Stuttgart possible starting lineup:.

Schalke are simply not scoring at home, and they could struggle here against an improving Stuttgart defence.

The visitors have struggled away in Gelsenkirchen over the years, but this is the perfect opportunity to improve that record.

  • A poll taken by Daily Mail Sport led to almost 2,000 votes from Chelsea fans, and 57.9 per cent were in favour of Mike Penders keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.
  • One is a 21-year-old Belgian yet to appear for his country and still in the early stages of what will hopefully be a highly promising career.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 05:36 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:52 EST, 19 November 2026.

A poll taken by Daily Mail Sport led to almost 2,000 votes from Chelsea fans, and 57.9 per cent were in favour of Mike Penders keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

One is a 21-year-old Belgian yet to appear for his country and still in the early stages of what will hopefully be a highly promising career. The other is a 34-year-old Argentinian who won the 2022 World Cup and has appeared 234 times in the Premier League.

We mention those brief backgrounds because when assessing who will give him the greater chance of stopping Leeds United from scoring on Saturday, Xabi Alonso takes them into account. Indeed, Alonso told us so while covering Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

One conversation with the manager was centred on his goalkeeper options. At that time, they were Penders and Robert Sanchez.

Alonso praised Penders’ potential but explained to us how highly he values ‘experience’ in his goalkeeper. ‘To have this security in goal is vital,’ he insisted when asked.

Sources indicate that sanchez was indeed nominated as his No 1 for their first fixture of the Premier League season at Fulham. The 29-year-old Spaniard had a stinker, which led to him being loaned to Como. It is a straightforward loan, and he has been second-choice to Jean Butez under Cesc Fabregas, so there is a chance he will be back at Chelsea next summer, but that is a problem for another day.

A Daily Mail Sport poll of almost 2,000 Chelsea fans resulted in 57.9 per cent voting in favour of Mike Penders (above) keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

Martinez is available for the first time since breaking his jaw at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Martinez arrived from Aston Villa for £7.5million, was told he would be Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper, and is now available again. He is able to play without a protective mask, as he did while representing Argentina in their 7-0 friendly win over Costa Rica on Tuesday night.

It was his first appearance since breaking his jaw at Everton and having surgery exactly a month prior. He headed back to London after that victory to return to Chelsea, presumably under the impression that he will be playing against Leeds come Saturday.

It is Alonso who will have the ultimate say on who goes in goal, in conjunction with his head of goalkeeping, Ben Roberts, and assistant goalkeeping coach, James Russell. That decision will be communicated with his chosen goalkeeper in the build-up, though Alonso is unlikely to tell us when we ask him at his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon.

One insider consulted this week mentioned his suspicion is the Argentinian will make an immediate return because it would create a headache for Alonso. Martinez is a big character, volatile, and, if reduced to second choice, would not be pleased.

Statistically, Leeds cross the ball more than most in the Premier League, which could be more challenging for Penders than Martinez.

Filling in for Martinez, Penders punched the ball into his own goal on his first league start for Chelsea in a 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur.

In a recent development, however, he impressed against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, then Manchester United and Sunderland in the Premier League. He won the Save of the Month award for October for denying Bryan Mbeumo at Stamford Bridge.

Penders won October's Save of the Month award for denying Man United's Bryan Mbeumo.

Penders is clearly a terrific talent, and it would be tempting to continue to show trust in him by having him face Leeds. Chelsea then face Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace, Liverpool and Manchester City in a rush of fixtures as we head into December.

It is a substantial decision to be made by Alonso, and would take bravery for him to stick with his prodigy in Penders, when we know the experience of the proven Martinez weighs heavy in his mind.

Chelsea vice captain Moises Caicedo is to be checked over at Cobham after a small injury scare while the influential midfielder was away with Ecuador.

Industry observers note that caicedo would be expected to wear the armband at Leeds in Reece James’ ongoing absence. He is set to return to the training ground on Thursday to be assessed.

The 25-year-old played 84 minutes in Ecuador’s first fixture of the break, a 2-0 victory against Costa Rica in which he scored. However, he then asked to be substituted at half-time of their 2-0 win over Bolivia, which ended in the early hours of Wednesday morning. Captaining his country, it was believed to be due to a small physical complaint.

Meanwhile, Chelsea have been looking at the midfield market in the build-up to this January after they missed out on bolstering their options in the summer when Enzo Fernandez was sold to Manchester City. They retain an interest in Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The understanding of how the Newcastle United recruitment team worked is based on myth and rumour.

Steve Nickson left on good terms for a more senior role.

All signings were approved or rejected by PIF with neither the Sporting Director, Eddie Howe or the recruitment team having any authority to make any financial decision.

That includes fees, wages and bonuses.

The allegation that Eddie Howe only wanted proven Premier League players is also a myth.

Here is the list January 2022 onwards whilst Eddie Howe was with Newcastle United: •Kieran Trippier (Atlético, £12m) •Chris Wood (Burnley, £25m) •Bruno Guimarães (Lyon, £40m) •Dan Burn (Brighton, £13m) •Matt Targett (Villa, loan) Summer 2022 •Targett (made permanent, £15m) •Nick Pope (Burnley, £10m) •Sven Botman (Lille, £35m) •Alexander Isak (Real Sociedad, £63m) •Loris Karius (free) •Garang Kuol (Central Coast Mariners) January 2023 •Anthony Gordon (Everton, £45m) •Harrison Ashby (West Ham, £3m) Summer 2023 •Sandro Tonali (Milan, £55m) •Harvey Barnes (Leicester, £38m) •Tino Livramento (Southampton, £32m+) •Lewis Hall (Chelsea, loan then £28m) •Yankuba Minteh (Odense, £6m) Summer 2024 •Lloyd Kelly (free) •Odysseas Vlachodimos (Forest, £20m) •William Osula (Sheffield Utd, £10m+) •John Ruddy (free) •Miodrag Pivaš (Jedinstvo Ub) •Vakhtang Salia (Dinamo Tbilisi, joined 2025) Summer 2025 •Anthony Elanga (Forest, £55m) •Malick Thiaw (Milan, £35m) •Jacob Ramsey (Villa, £40m) •Nick Woltemade (Stuttgart, £65m+) •Yoane Wissa (Brentford, £55m) •Aaron Ramsdale (Southampton, loan) •Antonio Cordero (Málaga, free) •Park Seung-soo (Suwon) Summer 2026 (before he left) •Ewen Jaouen (Reims) •Bazoumana Touré (Hoffenheim, £43m) •Sean Steur (Ajax) •Aladji Bamba (Monaco, signed 24 July).

Roughly £390m on players from English clubs and £420m on players from foreign clubs, about £810m in all.

An inconvenient truth when trying to support an anti Eddie Howe narrative – but factual.

Paolo Scaroni has insisted that AC Milan have a long-term project under Gerry Cardinale, for which the stadium is a vital component.

Industry observers note that as we wrote about at length last night, Cardinale has big looks to help get Milan back towards the top end of European football. The upcoming ‘MSE’ holding manufacturer is the latest development, while the Generali Stadium was recently unveiled, and other projects like the NBA Europe team are ongoing.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that it is all part of a mission to try and make the Rossoneri brand more than just a football club. Scaroni has been the face of the stadium project for many years, and he was a guest at a sports talk organised by RCS and entitled ‘Attracting foreign capital and enhancing the system for a real relaunch’.

It has been revealed that he spoke alongside Giovanni Carnevali (CEO and General Manager of Juventus), Giuseppe Marotta (President and CEO of Inter) and Ezio Maria Simonelli, (President of the Lega Calcio Serie A). His words are via MilanNews.

Industry observers note that serie A seems to be struggling compared to other Italian sports. What could be done to make football more competitive?

Recent findings suggest that “You’re telling me about something we’re doing, Gerry Cardinale’s idea. He came to the world of Italian football after twenty-five years in sport.

“It’s about creating Milan Sport Entertainment, that is, creating other sports around Milan, combining other sports with football, providing entertainment, communicating, and using Milan and Milano – because he also places great importance on the city of Milan, which is one of Europe’s emerging cities – to create an attractive environment for other sports and other situations.

“I’ll give just one example: if you take the United States, which is a gigantic market for the world of sports, football comes in fifth among the sports that Americans love, after basketball, of course, and even after hockey.

“So, how do we make football – and, in our case, Serie A – attractive in the United States? Precisely by creating this concept of entertainment around football, this concept of Milan, of fashion, of spectacle, that is, creating an attractiveness that competes with the other sports we compete with every day.

“This is the idea that Gerry brought in Italy, coming from his vast experience in the world of sport, and therefore around this we look to our future. Gerry Cardinale comes to say that he will never sell Milan, precisely because his project is a long-term one.”.

The Generali Stadium will be something more than a stadium and will help this….

According to recent reports, “Let’s say it’s been quite a complex journey. A very long one that I’ve been on with Inter since 2018-2019. But we’ve reached, let’s say, some key milestones. The first was in November last year, when we bought the San Siro stadium.

Sources indicate that “The Meazza belongs to Inter and Milan, and the entire surrounding area. So every now and then I read debates: ‘But should it be torn down, shouldn’t it be torn down?’. Well, this will be a decision we’ll make because it’s ours, so I want to say: we have a clear, notarial fact behind us that gives us ownership of the San Siro stadium.

Sources indicate that “This was the first step. The second was the presentation of the stadium that we held a few weeks ago. I think the Milanese and the professionals liked this presentation of this stadium designed by two great architects: one who worked on the exterior of the stadium and another who was responsible for the division of the spaces inside.

“Building a great stadium like this is something extremely key. Technical. Because then, as always when you tackle new topics, you learn things. I, for example, learned that Manica – this organization that designs our stadium – has built six hundred stadiums around the world.

“So, to say that building a stadium is a profession, it’s not something you improvise. And this was the second step. The third was that Generali seized the opportunity to own this latest stadium and the old one as well, because the collaboration on the Generali Stadium begins now.

“They seized the opportunity to have the two great Milanese clubs in Milan, both of which have a history of victories, are known worldwide and have millions of fans worldwide, and to use this latest stadium to promote their image, I would say especially in Europe – because Generali are a very European company – but I would also say worldwide.

It has been revealed that “They seized a great opportunity because opportunities like this are just the ones you get. And so I must say the negotiations concluded very successfully.”.

According to recent reports, “We have all the authorisations in front of us by September 2027. Therefore, in principle, we could begin construction of the upcoming stadium between the end of 2027 and the beginning of 2028. So, let’s say, we’re pretty close to the home stretch.

“Naturally, as always with these complications, there may be some discussion points. Furthermore, in Milan we’re heading towards an election campaign for a upcoming mayor, and a topic like the construction of a new stadium is one that can naturally excite politicians.

In a recent development, “Let’s say we’re confident because the entire process we’ve taken so far protects us from these potential disruptions, and we’re fiercely determined to move forward. With the new stadium, among other things, we’ll have €100 million in additional revenue.

“This €100 million in additional revenue is a fundamental ingredient for the success of AC Milan, Inter Milan, and Serie A around the world, because ultimately, €100 million – to have great players, to pay great players – is a fundamental ingredient for success.”.

Here, Sports Mole looks at how the Portugal international has performed against Liverpool during his professional career.

Fernandes has faced Liverpool on 13 previous occasions during his professional career, boasting a record of five wins, three draws and five defeats.

The attacker has scored three times against the Reds, in addition to contributing two assists.

Eleven of Fernandes' appearances against Liverpool have come in the Premier League, boasting a record of three wins, three draws and five defeats, scoring twice and registering two assists.

Fernandes has also faced Liverpool twice in the FA Cup, helping Man United to record a 3-2 win in the fourth round of the competition in 2021, finding the back of the net, before playing in a 4-3 success for the Red Devils in the quarter-finals in March 2024.

The Portuguese's two Premier League goals against Liverpool have been at Old Trafford, so he would create some personal history by finding the back of the net at Anfield on Sunday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Friday, we asked Newcastle United fans for 50 words on Bruno Guimaraes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Friday, we asked Newcastle United fans for 50 words on Bruno Guimaraes.

Saturday of course sees the former United captain return to St James’ Park.

Bruno Guimaraes and Arsenal on Tyneside for a 5.30pm Premier League kick-off.

Much has been stated about this return some three and a half months after deciding to leave.

We thought we would ask a number of Newcastle United fans for their thoughts,.

Rather than giving any leading pointers as to what to write, we totally left it up to the regular/irregular contributors to The Mag as to what they wanted to come out with.

We simply asked these Newcastle United fans ‘Please give us 50 words on Bruno Guimaraes’….

According to recent reports, trophy-winning captain who nearly cost us at Wembley when he went offside as Isak netted, then dallied on the ball and let Liverpool score. He profited professionally by joining us and we profited financially when he left. Loves to be the centre of attention, great drive, one to have in the trenches but don’t let him take a pen.

Bruno was what he was: part of the trio that jumpstarted this past half-decade of rejuvenation and triumph, the club’s heart and soul, and the technical genius that helped make the United midfield so imposing. I bear him no grudges for leaving or how, though doing so makes for better theatre. So now Bruno is what he is – another rival. Howay the lads!

Sources indicate that I find it hard not to harbour love for our former captain. He was an absolute hero during his time here. Like the ‘one that got away’ it hurts to see him with someone else. I wish him no luck at Arsenal but he’s a Newcastle legend for me.

Bruno joined a relegation fight with no relegation clause. He dragged us up the league, almost singlehanded at times. He gave everything for the club and for us and won us a trophy. Disgraceful rules dictate we can’t match his or many players ambitions. Saturday aside I wish him well.

He was the face of the exciting first phase after the takeover, a true top class player who could drag us to wins himself. He led us to glory which will was amazing but he tarnished his legacy on the way out after saying he wanted to be a legend.

Sources indicate that before the Arsenal game, let’s remember Bruno Guimarães as a footballer: brave in possession, relentless in the press, imaginative with the ball and wholehearted in every challenge. The disappointment of his leaving should not diminish what he helped create: belief, connection and a Newcastle side that made supporters dream again.

He lifted the trophy into the night sky at Wembley Stadium in March 2025, and for that he will always be a Newcastle United legend in my eyes. Did he blot his copy book with the move to Arsenal? Maybe, maybe not. Personally, I think the jogging bottoms he wore whilst paraded in front of an expectant audience at the Emirates were more offensive than his desire to leave us for them.

I like Bruno. He put more into my club than 95% of others. He captained us to the only trophy most fans have seen us win, and got us to the Champions League. That’s a good CV. Loyalty? Footballers are like us – loyal to family first. PL rules say we couldn’t double his wages. Arsenal could, and did, so he went. For his family. I won’t boo him.

(We had a great response to this request, so we have divided the replies into two separate articles, with part two to follow later today).

Enzo Maresca's side must bounce back on Saturday to avoid the possibility of Arsenal pulling further clear at the summit, as the Gunners could prove incredibly difficult to catch.

Man City have won each of their last 20 matches against Fulham in all competitions - a remarkable run - but their last three losses to the London club have come on home soil.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was the story of the summer, Bruno Guimarães moving from Newcastle United to Arsenal.

It was a saga that went on for weeks and weeks.

It felt like far longer than that.

For Newcastle United fans, this Bruno Guimarães to Arsenal saga felt very similar to the previous summer’s Alexander Isak to Liverpool one.

With the summer 2026 episode of transfer window torture, so much of it was played out in the media, claim and counter claim.

Now on the day that Bruno Guimarães returns with Arsenal to St James’ Park, there has been a media exclusive on ‘What really happened with Arsenal’s ‘multiple bids’?’.

Industry observers note that luke Edwards at The Telegraph giving this insight into what happened, stating: ‘It was the saga of the summer, with constant reports and claims from so-called experts that Arsenal made multiple bids for Guimarães that were rejected by Newcastle. The truth can be revealed now.’.

In his exclusive, Luke Edwards gives the following step by step detail of what happened with the Bruno Guimarães ‘multiple bids’ from Arsenal saga….

It has been revealed that ‘In July, Newcastle were shown a written offer from Arsenal by an intermediary. It was official looking, complete with Arsenal branding and said they would be willing to pay £45m for Newcastle’s captain.’.

In a recent development, ‘It was this document that was used to justify the constant stream of reports saying a bid had been made. Newcastle, though, were bemused. Not only was the fee offered derisory, but when they asked Arsenal to confirm the bid, they were greeted with silence for weeks. As a result, Newcastle dismissed it and maintained their “no bids” stance.’.

Sources indicate that ‘It is believed by some well-placed sources that the document had been acquired to pacify Guimarães, who was angry about the lack of progress being made. His representatives wanted to prove to him that Arsenal’s interest was genuine and they were working hard on his behalf. However, it was the key part of a tactic to feed into media pressure on Newcastle to sell.’.

‘There were no direct conversations between the clubs until the end of July. Even then, Arsenal continued to discuss numbers around the £50m mark, adding performance-related add-ons which Newcastle told them were unacceptable.’.

‘At the start of August, with Guimarães’s return to pre-season training looming and growing concern he could stay away, Newcastle issued an ultimatum. They would accept an offer of £75m paid in full, with no clauses. If Arsenal were not willing to pay it, Guimarães would not be sold. A deal was struck.’.

This enhancement fits in very much with what I have thought all along.

Whatever people want to believe about Bruno Guimarães, to me it was Arsenal to blame for most of this mess that blighted Newcastle United across summer 2026. If they had done things professionally from the start, it could and would have been a transfer that progressed very differently, rather than an embarrassing mess.

Recent findings suggest that instead of trying to use their friends in the media to force Newcastle United to sell on the cheap, Arsenal should have done things the correct way and made a formal approach to United at the very start. A transfer fee could have then been negotiated and the weeks and weeks of nonsense avoided.

Newcastle United will welcome Arsenal to St James' Park in the Premier League on Saturday evening.

Newcastle are 12th in the Premier League table, boasting 12 points from their opening 10 matches of the season, while Arsenal are at the head of the division, five points ahead of second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 5.30pm UK time on Saturday.

The Premier League match between Newcastle and Arsenal will be held at the former's home ground, St James' Park.

The corresponding game last season ended in a 2-1 victory for Arsenal, with Mikel Merino and Gabriel scoring late to secure all three points for the North London outfit.

The Premier League contest will be available on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League for viewers in the UK.

Sky customers can access the Premier League match on Sky Go and on the Sky Sports app, while it is also available via Now TV's Sports membership.

Sky Sports will show highlights, including any goals which have been scored, on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app.

Meanwhile, on Saturday, BBC One's Match of the Day programme will begin at 10.20pm and run until 11.45pm, with highlights of the match also available via that avenue.

Arsenal have won nine and lost one of their 10 Premier League matches this season, with 27 points leaving them five points clear at the top of the division.

Mikel Arteta's side recorded a 1-0 win over Hull City before the November international break, and they have been victorious in their last three matches in all competitions.

The likes of Brighton and Man City will be hoping for a favour from Newcastle in this match, as Arsenal are threatening to pull further clear at the top of the division.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough start to the season for Newcastle, with 12 points leaving them down in 12th spot in the division.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

First off, I need to start with an apology to anyone coming to The Mag to read my report on whatever happens/has happened against Arsenal, I have decided to allow the editor to flex his squad strength due to my not being there today, missing Newcastle United home matches is, for me at least, a difficult business.

I can already imagine some reading this are flabbergasted that someone with a ticket for a game against the Premier League champions would allow themselves to be otherwise occupied when they would crawl over broken all sorts to be there at any time.

The thing is, I’m a bit of a victim of poor prediction skills, as a look at any of my recent accas will confirm.

In a recent development, A few of my close mates were after arranging a meet up and a poll appeared in the WhatsApp group giving a choice of three weekends. One option was next week when I’m in Brighton, another was the untouchable territory of derby weekend and the remaining option was the Gunners at home.

I took a punt and committed to this weekend, knowing that if the game was shifted to Sunday (or any other mad weekend kick off that wasn’t Saturday) I’d be able to get to it, convincing myself we’d be the Sunday warm up to Liverpool v Man Utd.

So, it came to pass that wasn’t to be.

Ditch your old mates and head to the game, or give someone else a chance with your ticket?

Again, opinions will be polarised as some commentators will doubtless be about to say that they would chop their hand off with a rusty spoon to be in that ground, whereas many others will have found themselves in the position where they choose life over NUFC.

I haven’t made this kind of miscalculation very often, with most of my absences from Newcastle United home matches being early season when it’s clashed with a holiday.

Memories of enduring last season’s defeat to Liverpool in a bar at Disneyland Paris with an obnoxious cockney red mouthing off behind me are not amongst my most magical. It’s maybe a bit easier to swallow missing a defeat though.

In a recent development, I’ll always remember when my youngest son was born and I confidently thought to myself he’d arrive in plenty of time for me to get to the game with Norwich in about six days. Mrs S saw it quite differently and her reaction to the prospect of me leaving her with a newborn and two toddlers as she recovered from a c-section was, if I’m honest, a bit over the top. I stayed at home and checked online to catch the news of Dwight Gayle’s 96th minute hat-trick goal sealing an incredible 4-3 comeback win.

Honestly, during the whole Mike Ashley era it was a bit easier to give things a swerve. I remember hauling myself out of the house on a freezing Wednesday evening full of cold. After standing waiting for a bus that never came I had a word with myself and trudged off back to bed, deciding I could do without that 1-1 draw with Burnley. No monitoring the amount of unused tickets in those days.

According to recent reports, it still always feels wrong to me not to be there. I have a family diary planning app where anything we have planned gets instantly input. When the fixtures are confirmed they all get banged straight in, with a hasty update for each tranche of kick off fiddling the interfering TV companies inflict on us. Mrs S knows that any arrangements need to fit around this, i.e. if a day out is in the offing, check the planner and pick a weekend we are away.

Sometimes this isn’t possible of course, as things like weddings, birthdays and concerts can’t be flexed to accommodate the match with Coventry. This can lead to arguments of course, as a request to attend the wedding of her work colleague you’ve met twice could be deemed as insufficient reason for home game avoidance, but sometimes you need to pick your battles. If it’s the weekend of the Sunderland match then someone else is welcome to have your hunter’s chicken and profiteroles. Less commanding fixtures and you play the game of addressing life’s (other) priorities, as family, friends and work can all be more in need of your attention.

Recent findings suggest that I can offer my fans some solace in that I will be back for the next edition of The Mag Podcast. Unfortunately this means relying on Hutch and Simon to relay the details of how the game panned out, so I apologise in advance for any inaccuracies, meanderings and downright lies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

It has been revealed that rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

It has been revealed that the supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Industry observers note that carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Industry observers note that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

Sources indicate that it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Sources indicate that carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

Industry observers note that “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager remarked. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Recent findings suggest that marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

Recent findings suggest that united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

According to recent reports, it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick noted: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

Recent findings suggest that “But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

In a recent development, when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:00.

England should be seen as the favourites to win the UEFA Nations League ahead of the quarter-final draw, a former Three Lions striker has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Thomas Tuchel's side will learn their knockout fate on Friday morning when the draw for the last eight is held, and England head into the ceremony as one of the four seeded teams courtesy of finishing first in League A Group 3.

The Three Lions unexpectedly pipped world and European champions Spain to top spot courtesy of an engrossing 3-2 win over La Roja on Sunday, ending an unparalleled 43-game unbeaten run for Luis de la Fuente's side.

England will meet one of Belgium, Netherlands or Norway in the quarter-finals, while France, Portugal and Germany represent the other three Group A winners going for glory.

Despite the strength of the draw, former England striker Mark Hateley believes that Tuchel's men have made themselves the favourites to win the trophy for the first time, and also reserved special praise foe the goalkeeping heroics of James Trafford.

According to recent reports, asked if England are leading the charge for Nations League stardom, Hateley replied: "100%. That's the best I've seen England, or any team, play over a period of, say, 60 minutes.

"They were incredible: high press, press, press, press, going man for man, confident enough to go man for man at the back against the world champions, allowing your midfield players to jump up with the strikers.

“It was tremendous to watch, the very best we've seen from an England side for many, many years, honestly. It was superb. We went to 3-0, rightly so, and Spain never had a shot. Their first was 50 minutes in, in the second half.

According to recent reports, “Trafford must have thought 'this was a goddamn easy game.' The only time I think he was at fault was his starting position for the penalty, when Anderson brought the boy down. If his starting position had been higher, I think he'd have made the interception. That would be my only fault for the goalkeeper.

“If you’re a shot stopper, you’re a shot stopper - it’s just the other side of his game, where you're reading it and where you should be, playing as that sweeper.

"With the way we were pressing, the only ball really on for Spain was a ball in behind into the last third, which was empty for long periods. There was nobody there where I thought he could have been. But those are the things you pick up on and learn from.”.

England have only ever competed in the Nations League knockout stages once before in the inaugural 2018-19 edition, when they reached the finals courtesy of beating Spain and Croatia to first place in their group.

However, at a time when the Nations League Finals only comprised four teams, Gareth Southgate's side fell to a 3-1 loss to the Netherlands in the semi-finals, meaning that they are still awaiting their first knockout-phase win in the tournament.

England could only place third in the group stage of the 2020-21 tournament, before an embarrassing relegation to League B in the 2022-23 edition, although they swiftly returned to the top tier.

In the current format, England's record of five wins, one loss and 19 goals scored represented their best-ever performance in the group stage of the Nations League, fuelling the belief that the Three Lions can finally end their trophy drought in 2027.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 03:48 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 07:04 EST, 19 November 2026.

The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.

In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.

No doubt new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live.

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release.

In a recent development, in a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and indicated he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'.

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The upcoming boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

Alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.'.

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

Sources indicate that 'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'.

It’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9.

Conor McGregor announced that he would give employees at various businesses the day off.

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern.

Arsenal's Declan Rice could be another to be locked into the new GTA having previously spoken about how much gaming helps him switch off.

In a recent development, he told GQ: 'I can never sleep after night games. It’s impossible. I’ll be that wired. I'll play Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA. Anything. Just play with a load of my friends. Adrenaline, everything. You don’t really settle down.

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'.

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the upcoming game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor announced that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was launched.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously said: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

According to recent reports, 'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

Industry observers note that 'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'.

Sources indicate that 🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6: “Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the proposal.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ.

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game.

Recent findings suggest that 'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, noted with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a substantial one.'.

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

Sources indicate that 'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' mentioned Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'.

According to recent reports, latest York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall said. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'.

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the concern as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'.

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after big games.

Those issues appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony mentioned it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event.

Department store chain John Lewis mentioned it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Friday, we asked Newcastle United fans for 50 words on Bruno Guimaraes.
  • Saturday of course sees the former United captain return to St James’ Park.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Friday, we asked Newcastle United fans for 50 words on Bruno Guimaraes.

Saturday of course sees the former United captain return to St James’ Park.

Bruno Guimaraes and Arsenal on Tyneside for a 5.30pm Premier League kick-off.

Much has been noted about this return some three and a half months after deciding to leave.

We thought we would ask a number of Newcastle United fans for their thoughts,.

Rather than giving any leading pointers as to what to write, we totally left it up to the regular/irregular contributors to The Mag as to what they wanted to come out with.

We simply asked these Newcastle United fans ‘Please give us 50 words on Bruno Guimaraes’….

It has been revealed that I said it on The Mag Pod when he left; Bruno will be remembered as a club legend. Having said that, he’ll be booed today – and deservedly so. He wants a title to his name and that’s the price he’ll pay.

I bear no grudge towards Bruno. He’s among our greatest players in my lifetime and the talisman of the post-takeover era. Do I wish he’d stayed? Of course. Yet I see his decision to chase trophies as disappointing, not treacherous. Booing him would dilute our treatment of the real traitors: then we’re the ones who look pathetic.

This is a player who skippered us to a major trophy and that memory always remains a positive one. His leaving was not enjoyable, but was inevitable. He’s a huge miss. He’s old news now.

Bruno. Our talisman, our captain, the man who lifted our first trophy in generations. A legend? Perhaps, with time. But he engineered the worst kind of departure when we needed him most, betraying us, the fans who adored him. A man desperate to be loved by everyone, he risks being loved by no one. A legend and a traitor.

We loved you Bruno for putting your faith in NUFC. We loved the cheeky goal against Southampton. We loved your gurning and windmillIng after winning a meaningless throw-in. We loved your Brazilian bromance with Major Joe. We loved you. But Gloria Gaynor was right: just turn around now, cos you ain’t welcome any more. We will survive.

It has been revealed that courageous, leader, legend. One of my favourite players to ever pull on the shirt. If it wasn’t for him, we wouldn’t have achieved anything like what we have in the last 5 years. It hurt like hell when he left and I wish he didn’t. But, I get it. If we could’ve matched his ambition, he would’ve stayed. I wish him luck – but not when he’s playing us.

At the end of the day, players aren’t slaves or indentured servants and they have a right to move on. Having a long contract nowadays is more about maintaining value for a potential sale than it is about loyalty. I think Bruno loved the toon and I don’t see it as disingenuous that he kissed the badge. No doubt he looked around when rumours of interest from Arsenal began and wondered where the massive promises from the owners had gone and why Eddie was so disgruntled and other top players were on their way out. He wasn’t leaving the club he’d fallen in love with, he was leaving the club it was becoming!

Song for Saturday (if we’re winning):.
